summary: How the person reaches the Crew: the relay names them in its own frame, and the relay client stamps x-kiro-relay-user.
rule: The relay puts the verified Kiro user ID in the request head's user field, never in a header a client could send. The relay client sets x-kiro-relay-user on the request it hands to the Crew's web server, overwriting any value. The Crew honors the header only on requests from its relay client, in process or over a local channel authenticated with a secret the Crew holds, and strips it from everything else. On the local and Tailscale paths the Crew never honors it. On a personal Crew it honors it only when it names the owner. On a team Crew it takes the person as named.

cases.name: local request carrying the header
cases.crewDoes: strips it and treats the request as not relayed

cases.name: personal Crew, a user who is not the owner
cases.crewDoes: refuses. The relay should never send this, so it is a second check

value: The person's stable Kiro user ID, never an email address or a display name.
